lines.text: Every programmer writes bugs. Today you learn to hunt them down with an AI helper, and understand them.
Tell the AI what you expected, what actually happened, and what you already tried.
A clear bug report gets a clear answer.
Saying it does not work only gets a guess.
Copy the exact error message, including the line number and the error type.
Error messages are clues, not insults.
Ask the AI what the message means before you ask for a fix.
Never trust a fix until you run it yourself.
Test with normal values and a tricky one, like zero or an empty list.
If it still fails, tell the AI exactly what happened.
When it works, ask why the bug happened and write the reason in one sentence.
Ask for a hint first, not the full fixed program.
Next time you will spot the same bug on your own.
Meera wants her quiz to print the score, but Python shows an error instead.
The error message says line three, and the type of error is a TypeError.
That is two useful clues to give the AI.
The hint is good: Python cannot join text and a number with a plus sign.
But the suggested fix turns the number into a number again.
Meera runs it, and the very same error appears, so the fix fails the test.
Meera tells the AI exactly what happened when she tested the fix.
Now the AI explains the real cause and gives a fix that works.
She writes one sentence in her bug log: plus cannot mix text and numbers.
This is the debug loop that real programmers use every day.
Change one thing at a time, so you know which change fixed it.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
